Most of what I find interesting in the data I work with never makes it into a paper.
A descriptive pattern is often too small to build an article around, but too useful to
leave in a folder — and journal timelines mean that by the time a finding is public, the
election it describes is two years gone.

So this is where those go: short descriptive analyses of Danish politics on social media,
notes on measurement problems I have run into, and plots that answer a question someone
asked me over coffee.

Everything here is written in R and rendered with Quarto, so where it is useful I will
include the code.

```{r}
#| label: example-plot
#| echo: fenced
#| eval: false
#| message: false

# Example: posts are ordinary .qmd files, so R code runs and its output is
# rendered directly into the page.
library(tidyverse)

ads |>
  count(party, target_group) |>                      # aggregate ad counts per party
  ggplot(aes(x = target_group, y = n, fill = party)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Who each party targets", x = NULL, y = "Ads") +
  theme_minimal()
```
